text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Over five hundred informal miners at the tourmaline farm mine Neu-Schwaben near Karibib barred employees of the British-based Indigo Sky Gems from entering the site. Although the mine has been taken over by ISG, its managing director Chris Johnston had given assurances that small scale miners would not be evicted.
- Nasria insurance company is to pay out N$4 million to Tsumeb Corp Ltd today, to cover damages after the recent strikes.
- The two main suspects in the National Housing Enterprise's Katatura Single Quarters corruption scandal remain in custody after their appeal application for bail was refused.
- There may be a change in the law allowing traditional leaders access to political office.
